files.name: README.md
files.content:
# WhisperFlow

A **fully local, offline** speech-to-text → LLM processing pipeline. No cloud. No OpenAI. No external model services. No audio leaves the machine.

The orchestrator is a small **Python stdlib-only** CLI (no pip dependencies) that drives two compiled C++ backends via subprocess + HTTP — the same architecture llama.cpp upstream blesses via `examples/talk-llama`, reproduced in Python so the STT and LLM backends stay individually upgradeable.

---

## Why this exists

Cloud dictation tools (Wispr Flow, Superwhisper) send your audio to remote servers. For sensitive workflows — medical notes, legal dictation, development — that's a privacy non-starter. WhisperFlow keeps every byte of audio on the machine it was recorded on.

The project grew beyond a CLI transcription tool into a full **OS-level dictation daemon** with Wispr Flow feature parity: push-to-talk hotkeys, system tray, floating overlay, context-aware formatting, and text injection into any focused application.

The latest work (commit `d2c3dfe` — *"qwen 3 asr integration done"*) adds **Qwen3-ASR** integration, routing visual and audio features through specialized transformer checkpoints alongside the existing whisper.cpp path.

---

## Key features

- **Fully offline**: no internet required after setup — whisper.cpp + llama.cpp run as local binaries
- **Zero runtime pip dependencies**: the Python orchestrator is stdlib-only (verified in `pyproject.toml`)
- **Dual C++ orchestrator**: `whisper_flow/pipeline.py` runs whisper.cpp via subprocess and llama.cpp via HTTP server, behind abstract interfaces so either backend can be swapped
- **Qwen3-ASR integration**: latest commit `d2c3dfe` — routes visual and audio features through specialized transformer checkpoints
- **Wispr Flow feature parity**: push-to-talk daemon, floating overlay, system tray, context-aware app detection
- **Win32 SendInput text injection**: inject transcribed text directly into any focused application
- **Voice snippets**: automatic text expansion for frequently spoken shortcuts
- **Multiple LLM modes**: `summarize`, `correct`, `command`, `assistant`, `raw`
- **GUI progress notifier**: live Tkinter window showing transcription progress in real time
- **Sub-30s segment chunking**: longer audio is split into 30-second windows with aligned timestamps
- **Subtitle output**: SRT, WebVTT, and JSON subtitles with `HH:MM:SS,mmm` timestamps (`pipeline.py` lines 28–35)
- **77/77 unit tests passing** across 8 test modules

---

## Tech stack (from `pyproject.toml`)

- **Runtime**: Python 3.8+ (stdlib only — no pip runtime deps)
- **STT backend**: whisper.cpp (compiled C++ binary, driven via subprocess)
- **LLM backend**: llama.cpp (HTTP `llama-server`, with CLI fallback)
- **ASR (experimental)**: Qwen3-ASR transformer checkpoints (commit `d2c3dfe`)
- **Audio**: ffmpeg (16 kHz mono WAV normalization + fallback mic capture), arecord (ALSA, Linux), sounddevice
- **GUI**: Tkinter (stdlib)
- **OS daemon**: Win32 `SendInput` via ctypes, system tray
- **Config**: JSON + TOML (via `tomli`) + env vars + CLI flags
- **Testing**: pytest (77 tests across 8 modules)

---

## Repository

**[github.com/ParthVarekar/whisper_flow_clone_local](https://github.com/ParthVarekar/whisper_flow_clone_local)** · latest commit `d2c3dfe` — *"qwen 3 asr integration done"*

files.name: ARCHITECTURE.md
files.content:
# WhisperFlow Architecture

## The core decision: whisper.cpp (STT) + llama.cpp (LLM)

This is the correct local architecture today. llama.cpp does **not** support Whisper transcription — its audio support is for multimodal audio-LLMs (Qwen2.5-Omni, Ultravox, Voxtral, **Qwen3-ASR**) and it has **no** OpenAI-compatible `/v1/audio/transcriptions` endpoint (open issues #15291, #21852). whisper.cpp is the stable, official Whisper port.

Upstream itself blesses the split: whisper.cpp ships `examples/talk-llama` — a single binary that links both whisper.cpp (for STT) and llama.cpp (for the LLM). Our orchestrator (`whisper_flow/pipeline.py`) reproduces that architecture in Python so the two backends stay cleanly separable and individually upgradeable — see `ARCHITECTURE.md` for the full structural explanation of the C++ model split.

The latest commit (`d2c3dfe` — *"qwen 3 asr integration done"*) layers **Qwen3-ASR** on top, routing visual and audio features through specialized transformer checkpoints alongside the existing whisper.cpp path.

---

## Data flow

```
Mic / Audio File
   │
   ▼
ffmpeg normalize (16 kHz mono WAV)
   │
   ▼
whisper-cli  ← subprocess (whisper_flow/backends/whisper_cpp.py lines 44–50)
   │  transcript + segment timestamps
   │  sub-30s segment chunking, aligned timestamps
   ▼
llama-server  ← 127.0.0.1:8080 (HTTP /completion)
   │  summarized / corrected / command / assistant reply
   ▼
Win32 SendInput → injects into focused app
```

`whisper_flow/pipeline.py` is the dual C++ orchestrator: it runs whisper.cpp via subprocess and llama.cpp via HTTP server, both behind abstract interfaces (`backends/base.py`) so either backend can be swapped without touching the pipeline.

---

## Component responsibilities

```
┌─────────────┐    subprocess     ┌──────────────────────────────┐
│ audio.py    │  (whisper-cli)    │ whisper_cpp.py               │  STT backend
│  normalize  │ ────────────────► │  lines 44–50: subprocess     │  (TranscriptionBackend)
│  16kHz mono │                   │  wrapper, parses whisper-cli │
│  chunking   │                   │  output, GUI notifier        │
└──────┬──────┘                   └────────┬─────────────────────┘
       │ WAV path                          │ TranscriptionResult
       ▼                                    ▼
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ pipeline.py                                                  │
│  lines 28–35: SRT / WebVTT / JSON subtitle formatters        │
│  (HH:MM:SS,mmm timestamps)                                   │
│  sub-30s segment chunking + timestamp alignment              │
│  merge chunks + format outputs                               │
└────────┬─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
         │ transcript text
         ▼
┌──────────────────┐    HTTP                          ┌──────────────┐
│ prompts.py       │ ──────────────────────────────►  │ llama_cpp.py │ LLM backend
│  mode templates  │                                  │  /v1/chat/   │ (LLMBackend)
│  summarize/...   │ ◄─────────────────────────────── │   completions│
└──────────────────┘   JSON                          └──────────────┘
```

The transcription and LLM backends are **separable modules** behind abstract interfaces (`backends/base.py`). Swap either by implementing the ABC — the pipeline never imports a concrete backend type directly.

---

## Why subprocess + HTTP (not Python bindings)

- **Minimal dependencies**: orchestrator is Python stdlib-only. No `llama-cpp-python`, `whisper-cpp-python`, torch, or ctypes ABI risk.
- **Official builds**: uses the upstream CMake build system verbatim.
- **Debuggability**: each backend is a normal process you can run/inspect independently.
- **Separable upgrade**: bump whisper.cpp or llama.cpp without touching the other or the orchestrator.

---

## Sub-30s segment chunking

Long audio files are split into **30-second windows** before being handed to whisper.cpp; the orchestrator realigns segment timestamps across window boundaries so the final SRT/WebVTT/JSON output has continuous `HH:MM:SS,mmm` timestamps. The subtitle formatters themselves live at `pipeline.py` lines 28–35.

---

## Wispr Flow daemon layer

Beyond the CLI pipeline, WhisperFlow runs as an always-on OS daemon:

| Module | Responsibility |
|---|---|
| `hotkeys.py` | Push-to-talk (`Ctrl+Shift+Space`), command mode (`Ctrl+Shift+T`), toggle mode |
| `inserter.py` | Win32 `SendInput` text injection + clipboard swapping |
| `overlay.py` | Borderless transparent overlay with live audio volume bar |
| `tray.py` | System tray icon with cleanup-mode and writing-style toggles |
| `app_detect.py` | Detects active app (Slack, Outlook, VS Code, Cursor) for context-aware formatting |
| `snippets.py` | Voice-activated text expansion |
| `daemon.py` | Background service lifecycle |
| `history.py` | Local JSONL logging of all dictations + search |

files.content:
# StudyOS

A local-first progressive web app built to support **GATE 2027** preparation — covering **both the GATE CS (Computer Science) and GATE DA (Data Science & AI) papers** — with the feature set of a commercial SaaS tool. All data is stored in a local SQLite database via Prisma, and a **local LLM (Gemma 4 via llama.cpp on port 8081)** powers the AI Buddy. Your study history never leaves your machine.

Most exam-prep apps are glorified todo lists. StudyOS models the **full study lifecycle**: estimation, timed tests, syllabus tracking, goals, planning, notes, and content — all interconnected through a 13-model Prisma schema (verified in `prisma/schema.prisma` lines 13–190: `Goal`, `Subject`, `Topic`, `Question`, `TestAttempt`, `TestAnswer`, `StudySession`, `StudyTask`, `Note`, `Folder`, `Document`, `ChatSession`, `ChatMessage`).

Built for an audience of one (me), dogfooded daily for GATE 2027.

---

## The 8 modules

1. **Dashboard** — hero ring, stat cards, activity chart, focus areas
2. **Estimation** — radar chart, subject mastery vs target, recommendations
3. **Tests** — full config → live runner → results → history state machine with question palette
4. **Syllabus** — collapsible 18-subject cards with studied toggles, practice shortcuts, and **drag-and-drop topic prioritization** (`@dnd-kit/core` + `@dnd-kit/sortable`)
5. **Goals** — sliders with live impact panel
6. **Planner** — task CRUD with 3-state status cycle + session logging
7. **Content** — question bank with filters + markdown notebook library with PDF.js viewer
8. **AI Buddy** — chat assistant backed by the local Gemma 4 model

---

## Design system

A custom Superhuman-inspired design system with a warm aubergine/indigo-navy palette, pixel-matched to a reference screenshot through 3 iterative design audits for long-session readability.

---

## Tech stack

- **Framework**: Next.js 16 (App Router), React 19, TypeScript 5
- **Database**: Prisma 6 + SQLite (local file)
- **State**: TanStack Query (server) + Zustand (client)
- **Forms & validation**: React Hook Form + Zod
- **UI**: Tailwind CSS 4, shadcn/ui, Lucide, Framer Motion, Sonner (toasts)
- **Drag-and-drop**: `@dnd-kit/core` + `@dnd-kit/sortable` (custom topic prioritization)
- **Charts**: Recharts 2.15.4 (study pacing, accuracy, test attempt scoring)
- **Editor**: MDX Editor, React Markdown (explanations for MCQ/MSQ/NAT questions)
- **PDF**: pdfjs-dist 6
- **Local LLM**: Gemma 4 (`unsloth/gemma-4-E4B-it-GGUF`) via llama.cpp server on `localhost:8081` — see `LOCAL_MODEL_SETUP.md`
- **PWA**: custom service worker + manifest
- **Runtime**: Bun

---

## Repository

**[github.com/ParthVarekar/studyos](https://github.com/ParthVarekar/studyos)** · initial commit `26ad788` — *"feat: initial commit of StudyOS exam prep PWA"*

files.name: ARCHITECTURE.md
files.content:
# StudyOS Architecture

## Stack overview

```
[PWA — offline service worker]
      │
      ▼
[Next.js 16 App Router]
      │  TanStack Query (server state)
      │  Zustand (client state)
      ▼
[API Routes /api/subjects /api/topics /api/tests]
      │
      ▼
[Prisma ORM]
      │
      ▼
[SQLite — file:./db/custom.db]
      └── 13 models, 18 subjects, 91 topics
      │
      ▼  (AI Buddy)
[llama.cpp server — 127.0.0.1:8081]
      └── Gemma 4 (unsloth/gemma-4-E4B-it-GGUF)
```

---

## The 13-model Prisma schema

Verified in `prisma/schema.prisma` (lines 13–190). The schema models the full study lifecycle:

| Model | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `Goal` | Study goals with target mastery levels |
| `Subject` | 18 GATE subjects (seeded) |
| `Topic` | 91 GATE topics linked to subjects (seeded); drag-and-drop reorder via `@dnd-kit/sortable` |
| `Question` | Question bank entries (MCQ, MSQ, NAT) |
| `TestAttempt` | Test sessions with status state machine |
| `TestAnswer` | Per-question answers within an attempt |
| `StudySession` | Logged study time per topic |
| `StudyTask` | Planner tasks with 3-state status |
| `Note` | Markdown notes |
| `Folder` | Note organization |
| `Document` | PDF library entries |
| `ChatSession` | AI Buddy conversations (backed by local Gemma 4) |
| `ChatMessage` | Individual AI Buddy messages |

---

## Test runner state machine

The Tests module implements a full state machine:

```
config → running → results → history
```

- **config**: select subjects, question count, difficulty, question types (MCQ/MSQ/NAT)
- **running**: live MM:SS countdown timer, question palette showing per-question state (current/answered/flagged/unseen)
- **results**: score breakdown, per-question review, correct answers — visualized with **Recharts 2.15.4** for accuracy and pacing
- **history**: all past attempts with filters

Question types supported (each rendered with React Markdown for explanations):
- **MCQ** — single correct answer (radio)
- **MSQ** — multiple correct answers (checkbox)
- **NAT** — numerical answer type (numeric input)

Mutations invalidate the TanStack Query cache on submit/abandon/delete.

---

## Local LLM integration

The AI Buddy is powered by a **local LLM** rather than a cloud API — configured in `.env.local` and documented in `LOCAL_MODEL_SETUP.md`:

- **Model**: Gemma 4 (`unsloth/gemma-4-E4B-it-GGUF`) — a quantized GGUF file served by **llama.cpp**
- **Endpoint**: `http://127.0.0.1:8081/v1/chat/completions`
- **Why local**: keeps study conversations, notes, and doubt-solving fully on-device — same privacy posture as the SQLite store

---

## Dual GATE paper support

The schema and seeded syllabus cover **both** GATE CS (Computer Science) and GATE DA (Data Science & AI) papers, so the same install can drive either exam track.

---

## PWA + offline support

A custom service worker (`public/sw.js`) caches all static assets and enables full offline use. The app is installable as a PWA with a manifest. All data stays in the local SQLite file — no server required.

files.name: README.md
files.content:
# Nexus-AI

A 2D educational web game and User-Generated Content (UGC) platform designed to teach Python and MLOps through an immersive sci-fi narrative. Players step into the shoes of a space engineer writing **real Python code** to guide an AI companion.

Beyond the core campaign, Nexus-AI features a complete suite of creator tools — including a Level Editor and a Campaign Manager — empowering educators and developers to build, wire, and share their own custom coding challenges.

---

## Key features

- **In-Browser Python Sandbox**: `coding_game/js/editor/PythonWorker.js` runs a **sandboxed Pyodide Worker** — real CPython compiled to WASM — entirely in the browser. No server-side execution.
- **Synchronous `input()`**: `SharedArrayBuffer` + `Atomics.wait` let the worker pause until the main thread delivers input (`PythonWorker.js` lines 15–35) — true blocking input inside a Web Worker.
- **State-Based Validation**: `PythonWorker.js` lines 110–128 serialize the `pyodide.globals` namespace back to the game engine to verify challenge goals (e.g. `df.shape == (50, 4)` or `model_accuracy > 0.85`). Moves beyond brittle regex string-matching.
- **Auto-operator normalization**: `PythonRunner.js` lines 127–131 replace Unicode math symbols (`≥`, `≤`, `≠`) with standard Python operators (`>=`, `<=`, `!=`) before execution — so players can paste from formatted math worksheets.
- **10,000ms timeout**: `PythonRunner.js` line 7 terminates looping Python runs before they hang the tab.
- **2D Tile Level Editor**: A "2D Minecraft-style" grid builder with tools for painting geometry, placing interactive entities (Terminals, Portals, Bot Buddy), and a unique **Void brush** to carve organic, non-rectangular map shapes.
- **Custom Asset Pipeline**: Creators can upload `.png` or `.svg` files directly into the editor. Assets are converted to Base64 and embedded into the JSON save file.
- **n8n-Style Campaign Node Graph**: A custom, zero-dependency SVG visual routing system using dual-port symmetrical layouts and cubic Bezier curves to wire levels into branching campaigns.

---

## Tech stack

- **Frontend**: HTML5 · Vanilla JavaScript (ES6) · HTML5 Canvas · CSS3 (Glassmorphic UI). Zero heavy frameworks (no React/Vue/Angular).
- **Python Runtime**: Pyodide (WASM) running in a dedicated Web Worker (`PythonWorker.js`) to prevent UI blocking.
- **Synchronous primitives**: `SharedArrayBuffer` + `Atomics` (requires COOP/COEP headers).
- **IDE & Terminal**: CodeMirror 6 (editor) + Xterm.js (terminal)
- **Server**: Minimal Node.js static server (`coding_game/server.js` lines 36–44) — required strictly for setting COOP/COEP headers to enable `SharedArrayBuffer`.
- **Data Storage**: JSON files (`user_campaign.json`, `user_maps.json`) persisted to `localStorage`.
- **Audio**: Web Audio API (procedural SFX, no audio files)
- **No build system** — plain HTML/CSS/JS files

---

## Repository

**[github.com/ParthVarekar/coding_game](https://github.com/ParthVarekar/coding_game)** — default branch is `master` (not `main`). Clone, run `node server.js`, then open `http://localhost:3000`. Latest commit `b8de641` — *"docs: update Creator / User Guide image"*.

files.content:
# Nexus-AI Architecture

## Core Engine Freeze

The codebase enforces a strict boundary between the **Core Engine** (locked) and **Game Content** (data-driven JSON). This ensures stability — new levels and challenges are added via JSON, no JavaScript changes required.

### Locked core systems

- `coding_game/js/editor/PythonWorker.js` & `PythonRunner.js` — Execution Sandbox
- `coding_game/js/engine/Renderer.js`, `Camera.js`, `InputManager.js` — Game Loop & Hardware
- `coding_game/js/engine/MapManager.js` & `EntityManager.js` — Data processing logic
- `coding_game/js/utils/EventBus.js` — Communication Layer

---

## Data-driven content pipeline

All game content lives in JSON files:

### `data/curriculum.json`
Defines the Python challenges and dialogue:
- **Challenge ID**: unique key linked to terminals
- **Validation**: defines `expectedOutput` and `state` checks (logic-based, not regex)
- **Dialogue**: introduction and hint sequences

### `data/maps.json`
Defines the physical game world:
- **Grid**: 2D array of tile IDs (1: Floor, 2: Wall, 3: Hazard)
- **playerStart**: `{x, y}` spawn point
- **Entities**: array of interactable objects, each linking to a challenge via `challengeId`

---

## Pyodide execution pipeline

```
[CodeMirror 6 Editor]
      │  player writes Python (Unicode math symbols OK)
      ▼
[PythonRunner.js]
      │  line 7:   10,000ms timeout guard
      │  lines 127–131: normalize ≥/≤/≠  →  >=/<=/!=
      ▼
[Web Worker — PythonWorker.js]
      │  lines 15–35: SharedArrayBuffer + Atomics.wait
      │  blocks on input() until main thread delivers data
      ▼
[Pyodide WASM]  ← real CPython compiled to WASM
      │
      ▼
[pyodide.globals validation]  ← PythonWorker.js lines 110–128
      │  serializes globals back to game engine
      │  checks actual namespace state — NOT regex!
      ▼
[Canvas Engine — 60 FPS fixed timestep]
      ├── Camera lerping + screen shake
      ├── AABB tile collision
      └── EntityManager + NarrativeEngine
```

---

## Why COOP/COEP headers?

Pyodide's synchronous `input()` support requires `SharedArrayBuffer`, which browsers only enable when the page sends:
- `Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy: same-origin`
- `Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy: require-corp`

The Node.js server (`coding_game/server.js`, configured at lines 36–44) exists solely to set these headers. Without them, `PythonWorker.js` can't block on `input()` via `Atomics.wait`.

---

## Synchronous input via SharedArrayBuffer + Atomics

`PythonWorker.js` (lines 15–35) implements blocking input inside a Web Worker:

1. Worker calls `Atomics.wait` on a `SharedArrayBuffer` slot — execution pauses
2. Main thread writes the user's input into the shared buffer
3. Worker wakes via `Atomics.notify` and resumes Python execution

This is the only way to make Pyodide's `input()` work synchronously without freezing the UI thread.

---

## State-based validation

`PythonWorker.js` lines 110–128 serialize the `pyodide.globals` namespace back to the game engine after each run. The engine compares the resulting state against the challenge's `state` checks — for example:

```javascript
// Instead of: /result\s*=\s*42/
// We do:
const userVar = pyodide.globals.get('result');
return userVar === 42;
```

Players can solve challenges with any valid Python — the engine checks the *outcome*, not the *syntax*.

---

## Auto-operator normalization

`PythonRunner.js` lines 127–131 rewrite Unicode math symbols before execution:

| Input | Output |
|---|---|
| `≥` | `>=` |
| `≤` | `<=` |
| `≠` | `!=` |

This lets players paste expressions straight from formatted math worksheets or PDFs without syntax errors.

---

## UGC: Campaign Node Graph

The n8n-style campaign graph is a **zero-dependency** SVG system:
- **Dual-port symmetrical layout** — each level node has input and output ports
- **Cubic Bezier curves** — drawn dynamically to connect levels
- **Visual routing** — dictates where a level's Exit Portal transports the player next
- Creators drag levels onto the canvas, draw wires between ports, and publish to `localStorage`

# 2'nd_Brain

A local-first RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) knowledge base that ingests files, URLs, and pasted text into a **dual-store** architecture — SQLite for structured metadata and ChromaDB for vector search — then answers natural-language queries with streaming Server-Sent Events responses.

Note-taking apps don't reason over your notes. Cloud AI assistants don't keep your data private. 2'nd_Brain does both — locally.

> **Note**: The repo's `README.md` was just rewritten (commit `5e62b9e`) and is now comprehensive — pair this card with it for setup and usage.

---

## Key features

- **Dual-store architecture**: SQLite (metadata, memory, jobs) + ChromaDB (vector search)
- **Main FastAPI server**: `api.py` — every endpoint lives here, including the SSE streaming wrappers (lines 231–333) and the keyword-overlap graph builder (lines 110–123 schema, 212–222 edges)
- **Multi-source ingestion**: `core/pipeline.py` reads, chunks, and indexes files (token-bounded sliding window), URLs (with dynamic JS rendering via `ingestion/dynamic_scraper.py` — Playwright + playwright-stealth to bypass bot detection), and pasted text
- **Streaming SSE responses**: tokens stream to the frontend in real time via FastAPI `StreamingResponse` wrappers
- **Knowledge graph API**: `GET /graph` maps document, chunk, and memory nodes with keyword-overlap edges (overlap ≥ 0.2, capped at top-80 edges)
- **Auto-writeback**: after each query, a background worker summarizes and writes the conversation + sources back to SQLite
- **Background job tracking**: all ingestion tasks run as tracked background jobs
- **Multi-LLM support**: Gemini (cloud) or Ollama (local) — configurable

---

## Tech stack

- **Backend**: FastAPI, Python 3.x (verified via `requirements.txt`)
- **Vector store**: ChromaDB
- **Relational store**: SQLite (custom `db/sqlite_client.py`)
- **Embeddings / token counting**: tiktoken
- **LLM clients**: Gemini + Ollama
- **Web scraping**: Playwright + playwright-stealth + newspaper3k
- **HTTP client**: httpx
- **Config**: PyYAML
- **CLI output**: Rich
- **Frontend**: React 19 + Vite 8

---

## Repository

**[github.com/ParthVarekar/2-nd_Brain](https://github.com/ParthVarekar/2-nd_Brain)** · README refresh commit `5e62b9e`

files.name: ARCHITECTURE.md
files.content:
# 2'nd_Brain Architecture

## Dual-store design

The core architectural decision is the **dual-store split**:

- **SQLite** — structured metadata (document records, conversation memory, background job tracking)
- **ChromaDB** — vector embeddings for semantic similarity search

This separation lets each store do what it's best at: SQLite handles transactional metadata and relations, ChromaDB handles high-dimensional vector search. Neither store alone is sufficient for a production RAG system.

The whole backend is a single FastAPI server in `api.py` — every endpoint, the SSE streaming wrappers, and the graph builder all live there.

---

## Ingestion pipeline

```
[File / URL / Pasted Text]
      │
      ▼
[core/pipeline.py]
      │  reads, chunks (token-bounded sliding window), embeds
      ▼
[DynamicScraperManager]  ← ingestion/dynamic_scraper.py
      │  Playwright + playwright-stealth (bypasses bot detection on JS-heavy sites)
      │  handles JS-heavy pages, quality scoring,
      │  dynamic content detection, telemetry
      ▼
[Chunk + Embed (tiktoken)]
      ├──→ [ChromaDB]  (vectors)
      └──→ [SQLite]    (metadata + job tracking)
```

`core/pipeline.py` is the ingestion entry point: it reads the source, splits it with a **token-bounded sliding window** (tiktoken counts), and indexes the chunks into both stores. The `DynamicScraperManager` (in `ingestion/dynamic_scraper.py`) is the most complex ingestion component:
- Uses Playwright with `playwright-stealth` to bypass bot detection
- Detects whether a page needs JS rendering or can be scraped statically
- Scores content quality before persisting
- Falls back gracefully with content-length validation

---

## Query pipeline (streaming SSE)

Implemented in `api.py` lines 231–333 as FastAPI `StreamingResponse` wrappers emitting Server-Sent Events:

```
[User query (natural language)]
      │  POST /query
      ▼
[Embed query]
      │
      ▼
[Vector search → ChromaDB]  (top-k relevant chunks)
      │
      ▼
[Prompt Builder]  (system prompt + retrieved context + query)
      │
      ▼
[Gemini / Ollama]  ← streaming via StreamingResponse (SSE)
      │  tokens stream via SSE
      ▼
[React frontend]  (live token rendering)
      │  after stream ends
      ▼
[background write-back worker]  → [SQLite]
      │  summarizes + persists conversation memory + sources
```

The **post-stream auto-write-back** runs in a background worker: after the SSE stream closes, the worker summarizes the conversation and writes the updated memory + sources back to SQLite. This is decoupled from the live stream — the user sees their answer immediately, and the memory persistence happens after the stream closes. This avoids any race condition between streaming and database writes.

---

## Knowledge graph endpoint

`GET /graph` builds a force-graph payload for the frontend visualization. The implementation lives in `api.py`:

- **Graph schema** — `api.py` lines 110–123 define the node and edge types:
  - **Document nodes** — one per ingested document
  - **Chunk nodes** — one per text chunk (linked to parent document)
  - **Memory nodes** — one per past conversation/query
- **Edges** — `api.py` lines 212–222 compute keyword-overlap connections:
  - Edge weight = set-intersection score between documents / memory entries
  - Edge only created when **overlap ≥ 0.2**
  - Capped at **top-80 highest-weight edges** for visualization performance

The `_build_graph_payload()` function in `api.py` assembles this structure from SQLite.

---

## Background job tracking

All ingestion tasks (file, URL, text) run as tracked background jobs:
- Each job has a status (pending, running, completed, failed)
- The frontend polls job status
- Failed jobs surface their error messages
- This keeps the API responsive while heavy ingestion (scraping, embedding) runs async

files.content:
# Agent Safety Net

A **Manifest V3 Chrome extension** that acts as a runtime safety layer for browser-based AI agents. It intercepts all outbound network requests made by AI agents in your browser, runs local PII and prompt-injection detection, and presents a four-tier intervention UI — all without sending your data anywhere.

Browser-based AI agents (ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini web) can read your DOM and make outbound requests — including your personally identifiable information. There's no runtime safety layer inspecting what leaves your browser. Agent Safety Net fills that gap.

> **Note**: This repo ships **no root `README.md`** — the source-of-truth docs are `PRODUCT_SPEC.md`, `ARCHITECTURE_V2.md`, and `BUILD_PLAN.md` at the repository root. Treat those as the canonical references.

---

## Key features

- **MAIN world payload interception**: `src/injected/index.ts` monkey-patches `window.fetch` and `XMLHttpRequest` in the page's MAIN execution world, bypassing `declarativeNetRequest`'s inability to inspect request bodies
- **3-hop relay**: `postMessage` (MAIN → content script) → `chrome.runtime.sendMessage` (content script → Service Worker at `src/background/index.ts`) — payloads cross three isolation boundaries before detection runs
- **Local rule engine**: `src/rules/pii-detection.ts` (fast regex pattern arrays for credit cards and emails) and `src/rules/prompt-injection.ts` (blocks four major injection families — `ignore`, `disregard`, `jailbreak`, `developer mode` — at lines 6–11, with recursive base64 decoding for obfuscated payloads) run entirely in the Service Worker — no cloud calls
- **Anomaly detection**: `src/rules/anomaly.ts` monitors API endpoint counts and request timings for drift
- **Sub-millisecond detection**: average latency of **0.011ms per request**, ~90,000 req/sec throughput, with an in-memory LRU cache for O(1) repeated lookups
- **4-tier intervention UI**: Allow (silent) / Warn (toast) / Confirm (modal) / Block (full-page interstitial) — injected into the page based on the rule engine's verdict
- **Intent-drift detection**: tracks multi-step behavioral sequences (e.g. sensitive DOM read → unrecognized outbound POST within 5 seconds) as a stateful signal
- **Gemini Flash**: used **only** for async post-block explanations in plain English — never for the detection itself

---

## Tech stack

- **Extension platform**: Chrome Manifest V3
- **Build**: Vite + custom `build.mjs`
- **Language**: TypeScript
- **UI framework**: React 19 + React DOM 19
- **Styling**: Tailwind CSS
- **Detection**: `tiny-lru` (cache), Google Safe Browsing API v4 (optional), Gemini Flash API (post-block explanations only)
- **Type defs**: `@types/chrome`

---

## Repository

**[github.com/ParthVarekar/agent_safety_net](https://github.com/ParthVarekar/agent_safety_net)** · latest commit `818ef5b` — *"1.02.01 (fixed rate limiting and tried to optimise)"*

files.name: ARCHITECTURE.md
files.content:
# Agent Safety Net Architecture

## The interception pipeline

The core challenge: Chrome's `declarativeNetRequest` API **cannot inspect request bodies** — it only sees headers and URLs. To detect PII or prompt injections in what an AI agent is *sending*, we need to intercept the payload itself.

The solution is **MAIN world script injection** in `src/injected/index.ts`, followed by a 3-hop relay to the Service Worker:

```
[Page MAIN world — src/injected/index.ts]
      │  monkey-patch window.fetch
      │  monkey-patch XMLHttpRequest.open
      ▼  window.postMessage            ← HOP 1
[Content script (isolated world)]
      │  chrome.runtime.sendMessage    ← HOP 2
      ▼
[Service Worker — src/background/index.ts]
      ├── src/rules/pii-detection.ts       ← regex arrays (CC, email)
      ├── src/rules/prompt-injection.ts    ← 4 families, base64 decode
      ├── src/rules/anomaly.ts             ← endpoint count + timing drift
      ├── tiny-lru                         ← O(1) domain/hash cache
      └── intent-drift                     ← sequential chain detection
      │  verdict
      ▼
[4-tier intervention UI]
      ├── Allow   (silent)
      ├── Warn    (toast)
      ├── Confirm (modal)
      └── Block   (full-page interstitial)
      │  (on Block, async)
      ▼
[Gemini Flash]  ← plain-English explanation only
```

---

## Why MAIN world injection?

Chrome extensions run content scripts in an **isolated world** — they can see the DOM but not the page's JavaScript context. `window.fetch` and `XMLHttpRequest` belong to the page's MAIN world.

To monkey-patch them, the extension uses `chrome.scripting.executeScript` to inject `src/injected/index.ts` into the MAIN world. That script:
1. Saves references to the original `fetch` and `XMLHttpRequest.open`
2. Replaces them with wrappers that capture the request payload
3. Relays the payload via `window.postMessage` to the isolated content script (HOP 1)
4. The content script forwards it to the Service Worker via `chrome.runtime.sendMessage` (HOP 2)
5. The Service Worker (`src/background/index.ts`) runs detection and returns a verdict

Three isolation hops keep the page's JS context fully separated from the rule engine.

---

## The rule engine

Detection runs entirely locally in the Service Worker:

| Module | Purpose | Latency |
|---|---|---|
| `src/rules/pii-detection.ts` | Fast regex pattern arrays for credit cards and emails | <0.5ms |
| `src/rules/prompt-injection.ts` | Blocks `ignore`, `disregard`, `jailbreak`, `developer mode` (lines 6–11); recursive base64 decode for obfuscated injections | <0.5ms |
| `src/rules/anomaly.ts` | Monitors API endpoint counts and request timings for drift | event-driven |
| `tiny-lru` | In-memory LRU cache for O(1) repeated domain/hash lookups | <0.1ms |

Benchmark: average **0.011ms per request**, ~90,000 req/sec throughput, 11.03ms total for 1,000 iterations under burst load.

---

## Prompt-injection rule families

`src/rules/prompt-injection.ts` (lines 6–11) defines four major injection families that are blocked outright:

1. **ignore** — *"ignore previous instructions"* style attacks
2. **disregard** — *"disregard the above"* overrides
3. **jailbreak** — well-known jailbreak templates
4. **developer mode** — fake system / developer-role escalation

For obfuscated payloads (e.g. base64-encoded injections), the rule applies **recursive base64 decoding** until either plain text emerges or a depth limit is hit, then re-runs the family matchers.

---

## Intent-drift detection

Beyond single-request analysis, `src/rules/anomaly.ts` and the intent-drift layer track **sequential behavioral chains**:

- A "sensitive DOM read" (e.g. reading a form with PII) followed by
- An "unrecognized outbound POST" within 5 seconds

This stateful signal is persisted to `chrome.storage.local` to survive Service Worker wakeup cycles (MV3 Service Workers are ephemeral and can be killed between requests).

---

## 4-tier intervention UI

Based on the verdict, the extension injects one of four UI responses into the page:

1. **Allow** — silent, request proceeds (logged for audit)
2. **Warn** — non-blocking toast notification
3. **Confirm** — blocking modal requiring user click
4. **Block** — full-page interstitial, request blocked

On Block, the extension asynchronously calls Gemini Flash to generate a **plain-English explanation** of why the request was blocked — this is the only cloud call, and it happens after the block, not before.

# Shorts Intelligence OS

A multi-agent CLI and FastAPI backend for analyzing YouTube Shorts content and generating production-ready scripts. It scores viral potential, forecasts retention at four checkpoints, performs competitor analysis, and produces scene-by-scene scripts with editing instructions — all driven by **15 formally specified metrics** and a 12-agent pipeline coordinated by a central orchestrator.

Short-form video is the dominant content format, but creators fly blind — no formal metrics for viral potential, no retention forecasts, no structured way to learn from what works. Shorts Intelligence OS treats Shorts analysis as an engineering problem with documented formulas and confidence levels.

---

## Key features

- **12 specialized agents** in `backend/core/agents/` — Audience Psychologist, Concept Selector, Viral Pattern Extractor, editor, script_writer, competitor_research, audience_psychologist, visual_intelligence, and more — coordinated by `backend/core/orchestrator.py`
- **15 formally specified metrics**: viral score, retention forecasts at 3s/10s/20s/completion, calibration error, learning score, pattern confidence, critic agreement, and more — each with a documented formula, unit, and confidence level
- **Visual Intelligence agent** (`backend/core/agents/visual_intelligence.py`): runs the **local Qwen2.5-VL-7B** model for visual pacing, frame timelines, and retention indices
- **NVIDIA NIM client** (`backend/core/nim_client.py`): queries **Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct** models for high-value reasoning with paced scheduler, exponential backoff, request deduplication, and response caching
- **Retention forecasting**: predicts drop-off at 3s, 10s, 20s, and completion percentage using documented formulas
- **SSE progress streaming**: live progress events from the FastAPI backend to the Next.js frontend
- **Persistent memory**: SQLite stores every analysis run + NVIDIA NIM response cache
- **FAISS pattern learning**: vector store accumulates learned patterns across analysis runs
- **Video telemetry**: automated download scripts scrape TikTok / YouTube Shorts metadata and compute per-frame retention rates
- **Shared memory agent workflow**: synchronous feedback loops use `SharedArrayBuffer` + `Atomics` so agents can wait on each other mid-pipeline
- **Scene-by-scene scripts**: full editing instructions, thumbnail ideas, and AI generation prompts

---

## Tech stack

- **Backend**: FastAPI, uvicorn, Pydantic (contracts documented in `API_CONTRACTS.md`)
- **CLI entry point**: `backend.core.cli:main` (via `shorts-agent` script)
- **Orchestrator**: `backend/core/orchestrator.py` — central coordinator driving the 12-agent pipeline
- **Python**: ≥3.11
- **NVIDIA NIM**: custom `backend/core/nim_client.py` querying **Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct**
- **Local vision model**: Qwen2.5-VL-7B (`backend/core/agents/visual_intelligence.py`)
- **Optional local LLM**: llama.cpp (binaries in `llama.cpp_bin/`)
- **Memory**: SQLite (`data/shorts_memory.sqlite`, `data/nim_cache.sqlite`)
- **Pattern learning**: FAISS (`vector_store/` directory)
- **Frontend**: Next.js 15, React, Tailwind CSS
- **Multimodal**: vision analysis (`test_vlm.py`, `benchmark_vision.py`)

---

## Repository

files.content:
# Shorts Intelligence OS Architecture

## Multi-agent pipeline

```
[Input: transcript + metadata + analytics + video telemetry]
      │
      ▼
[FastAPI backend]  ← uvicorn
      │  SSE progress stream
      ▼
[Orchestrator — backend/core/orchestrator.py]
      │  coordinates 12 specialized agents in backend/core/agents/
      ▼
[12-agent pipeline]
      ├── Audience Psychologist   → viewer personas
      ├── Concept Selector        → core idea extraction
      ├── Viral Pattern Extractor → pattern mining
      ├── competitor_research     → baseline deltas
      ├── visual_intelligence     → Qwen2.5-VL-7B frame analysis
      ├── editor                  → cut/pacing decisions
      ├── script_writer           → scene-by-scene blueprint
      ├── ... (5 more specialized agents)
      │
      ▼
[15 metrics: viral score, retention 3s/10s/20s,
   calibration error, critic agreement, ...]
      │
      ▼
[Memory layer]
      ├── SQLite (shorts_memory + nim_cache)
      └── FAISS (pattern retrieval)
      │  (optional, high-value)
      ▼
[NVIDIA NIM — backend/core/nim_client.py]
      └── Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
      │  paced scheduler + backoff + cache
      ▼
[Next.js frontend]  ← structured Markdown report
```

The orchestrator drives agents through **synchronous feedback loops** backed by `SharedArrayBuffer` + `Atomics`, so a downstream agent can block until an upstream agent publishes its slice — no polling, no race conditions.

---

## The 15-metric system

`SYSTEM_METRICS.md` defines each metric with:
- **Formula** — the exact computation
- **Unit** — percentage, score (0-100), count, etc.
- **Confidence level** — one of:
  - `Observed Truth` — directly measured from data
  - `Inferred Pattern` — derived from observed patterns
  - `Speculative Hypothesis` — model-based estimate
- **Update trigger** — when the metric recalculates

### Example: retention_3s formula

```
retention_3s = clamp(72 + hook_strength × 0.24 + novelty_score × 0.05)
```

This forecasts what percentage of viewers will still be watching at the 3-second mark, based on the hook strength and novelty scores.

---

## Visual Intelligence agent

`backend/core/agents/visual_intelligence.py` runs the **local Qwen2.5-VL-7B** vision-language model to compute:
- Visual pacing across frame timelines
- Per-frame retention indices
- Thumbnail / hook frame candidates

It feeds its outputs back into the 15-metric system as `Observed Truth` signals.

---

## NVIDIA NIM integration

`backend/core/nim_client.py` is a custom client for the NVIDIA NIM API, querying **Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct** for high-value reasoning where a larger model meaningfully improves output quality. To stay within rate limits, it uses:

- **Paced request scheduler** — spaces out requests to avoid burst-rate limits
- **Exponential backoff** — retries with increasing delay on 429s
- **Request deduplication** — identical prompts aren't sent twice
- **Response caching** — NIM responses cached to `data/nim_cache.sqlite`

All request/response shapes are documented as Pydantic models in `API_CONTRACTS.md`.

---

## Video telemetry

Automated download scripts scrape TikTok and YouTube Shorts metadata and compute per-frame retention rates, which feed the `Observed Truth` retention metrics (`retention_completion`, pacing score, SVSA/AVD estimates).

---

## Schema evolution

A real bug was patched: the LLM sometimes generated script segments without required keys. The fix enforced a canonical `ScriptSegment` schema with safe dict access across all agents:

```python
# Before (buggy): segments could be missing keys
for seg in segments:
    print(seg['text'])  # KeyError if missing

# After (safe): canonical schema enforced
segment = ScriptSegment(**safe_dict(seg))
print(segment.text)
```

---

## Memory & learning

Each run writes to two SQLite databases:
- `shorts_memory.sqlite` — analysis results, creator baselines, learned patterns
- `nim_cache.sqlite` — cached NIM responses

FAISS (`vector_store/`) indexes pattern embeddings for similarity retrieval across runs — so the system learns what works over time.

files.content:
# Results & Verification

## The 15-metric system

All metrics are formally specified in `SYSTEM_METRICS.md` with formulas, units, confidence levels, and update triggers:

| Metric | Confidence Level |
|---|---|
| Viral score | Inferred Pattern |
| Retention @ 3s | Speculative Hypothesis |
| Retention @ 10s | Speculative Hypothesis |
| Retention @ 20s | Speculative Hypothesis |
| Retention @ completion | Observed Truth |
| Calibration error (MAE + RMSE + signed bias) | Observed Truth |
| Learning score | Inferred Pattern |
| Pattern confidence | Inferred Pattern |
| Critic agreement | Observed Truth |
| Hook strength | Inferred Pattern |
| Novelty score | Inferred Pattern |
| Pacing score | Observed Truth |
| SVSA/AVD estimates | Observed Truth |
| Sentiment | Observed Truth |
| Competitor delta | Observed Truth |

---

## Agent inventory (12 agents)

All 12 specialized agents live in `backend/core/agents/` and are dispatched by `backend/core/orchestrator.py`:

| Agent | Role |
|---|---|
| `audience_psychologist` | Viewer personas, attention hooks |
| `concept_selector` | Core idea extraction |
| `viral_pattern_extractor` | Pattern mining from history |
| `competitor_research` | Baseline deltas vs. peers |
| `visual_intelligence` | Qwen2.5-VL-7B frame analysis |
| `editor` | Cut/pacing decisions |
| `script_writer` | Scene-by-scene blueprint |
| + 5 more specialized agents | (router, extraction, quantitative, qualitative, idea generator) |

The `visual_intelligence` agent runs the **local Qwen2.5-VL-7B** model; high-value reasoning is offloaded to **Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct** via `backend/core/nim_client.py`.

---

## Benchmarking

`BENCHMARK_RESULTS.md` documents Phase 1 results:
- Win rate vs. baseline LLM: measured (documented as baseline, not a performance claim)
- Category averages: tracked across multiple analysis dimensions
- The system is positioned as a measurement framework, not a guaranteed viral predictor

---

## Testing & smoke tests

- `scripts/smoke_test.py` validates end-to-end functionality including:
  - SSE progress streaming
  - Report generation
  - Schema enforcement (ScriptSegment)
- `STARTUP_GUIDE.md` documents setup and known failure modes
- `test_vlm.py` + `benchmark_vision.py` — multimodal vision analysis tests

---

## Documentation suite

- `SYSTEM_METRICS.md` — 15 metric definitions
- `API_CONTRACTS.md` — Pydantic request/response models
- `BENCHMARK_RESULTS.md` — Phase 1 results
- `STARTUP_GUIDE.md` — setup + common failures
- Architecture audits + validation reports
- ~70% complete per research — core pipeline functional, ongoing content/feature additions
